claim: A width byte does not hold the number the page prints against it. It indexes five entries and they are the printed figures halved -- 0.25, 0.5, 1.0, 2.0 and 4.5 -- put into the section as the width its bandwidth is defined by at the half-gain points, which is the form the era's filter arithmetic is written in. Settings past the fifth return what the first returns, which on this slot is also the entry it powers up in, so the two cannot be told apart from these takes. A fourth type carrying the same printed table tells them apart by disagreeing with both: its byte powers up at the third entry and everything past the fifth returns the fifth, so which entry a byte outside the printed steps comes back at is a property of the slot and not of the table. The five entries do not depend on where the peak is: the same table answers with the centre at the bottom of its own table and with it in the middle, and the two mid sections of the type answer alike.
why_not_named: A width and a bandwidth in octaves are two spellings of the one coefficient a section takes, and each converts into the other exactly. Nothing measured here separates them, so the claim is about the coefficient and the entries are reported in the spelling the page uses.

measurements.why: The width byte swept at all five printed settings and at three past them, with the gain it shapes at full and the centre in the middle of its table. The three settings past the fifth are what say the table has five entries and no bound check.

The same byte at the same settings with the centre at the bottom entry of its own table instead. This is what makes five numbers a table rather than five coefficient sets stored against one centre, and it is the record that tells the last entry's two readings apart, because at this centre the table's entry and the unit's peak stand in one band.
The type's other mid section, at three of the five settings. Three is what asking whether the two sections answer alike costs; it is not a second reading of the table.

The mid section printed inside a combination type, read at the same five settings with the type's other stages written off. Not scored in the ranking -- the models are rendered through the standalone type -- and carried because its five half-power spans are the standalone type's.

The same section in a second combination type, which prints it five addresses lower. Read with its centre byte at the setting the standalone type's own width run held, so its half-power edges can be laid over that run's without a correction, and they are the same bands at all five settings.

document_rows.read_as: Evidence that a page prints five figures against eight slots, and nothing about the unit. What the claim takes from them is that there are five of them and that the list is the same at every slot. It does not take the figures: the measurement says the section holds half of each, which is the whole of what this claim adds to the page.

era_priors.claim: A width byte of this period indexes a short table and the settings past its end have no bound check.
era_priors.why: Five printed values against a byte that takes a hundred and twenty-eight is an index, and a table written in the era's assembly is read without a range test. What that predicts is not a clamp: a byte past the end reaches whatever the fallback is, and here all three settings asked past the fifth return the first entry, which is also the entry this slot powers up in.
era_priors.would_be_wrong_if: A setting past the fifth returned a width none of the first five return, or returned the fifth rather than the first.

era_priors.claim: What a table entry holds is the reciprocal the section's arithmetic wants, not the figure a musician reads.
era_priors.why: The biquad every part of the period computes reaches its section through one intermediate quantity -- half the sine of the centre's angle divided by the width -- so what is cheapest to store is one over twice the width, and the factor between what is stored and what is printed is then a property of which two points on the curve each was defined between rather than of the table.
era_priors.would_be_wrong_if: The measured entries stood in no fixed ratio to the printed ones, which would make the page's list and the unit's two unrelated tables rather than one read two ways.

era_priors.claim: One width table serves every centre, rather than a set of coefficients being stored per centre and per width.
era_priors.why: Sixteen centres against five widths is eighty coefficient sets if they are stored and one multiply if they are not. The era buys the multiply.
era_priors.would_be_wrong_if: The same setting returned different widths at two centres, at a resolution the run can tell apart.

adds: The records say where each setting's profile has fallen to half its peak. That is a pair of frequencies and not a width: it is quantised to the band set, it is read off a profile a band-energy reading has already smoothed, and on the narrowest setting the smoothing widens the peak enough to read a section of 4.5 as one of 4.2. This claim is the step from those pairs to the number the section holds, made by rendering each candidate table through the same takes and the same reading the unit's own profile went through, so that whatever the band set does to a narrow peak it does to both sides. What it adds over the page is that the page's figures are twice the section's.

alternatives.reading: The five entries are the figures the page prints: 0.5, 1.0, 2.0, 4.0 and 9.0.
alternatives.ruled_out_by: Scored against the same seven records it comes back with a median residual 7 times the winner's over the span the byte commands, and it leans on two of the three records that carry a feature where the winner leans on none. At the widest setting it puts half as much of the profile over half the peak as the unit does -- thirty bands against the unit's forty-nine -- which is not a residual to be weighed but a different curve.

alternatives.reading: The page's figures with the last rounded to the doubling the first four make: 0.5, 1.0, 2.0, 4.0, 8.0.
alternatives.ruled_out_by: It differs from the printed table at one entry and falls with it everywhere else, for the same reason and by the same margin.

Carried to bracket the winner from the other side, and beaten by more than the printed table is: its widest entry is narrower than the winner's narrowest but one, and its narrowest is under one band of this reading, which the record says it cannot hold.

alternatives.reading: The last entry is 4.0 rather than 4.5 -- a table that doubles all the way from a quarter, with the page's ninth a printed figure and not a stored one.

separated_by.observable: The band profile at the narrowest setting, at the bands the peak has a flank in.

predicts.4.0: The same peak eleven per cent wider, which is at most 0.61 dB of profile at one band and nothing at the top.

separated_by.sensitivity_here: At the centre the run swept at the bottom of the frequency table the two are told apart at 14 bands, the widest gap is 0.61 dB where the run's own repeats stand 0.17 dB apart, and the unit sits nearer 4.5 at every one of them: 0.204 dB against 0.544 dB. At the centre in the middle of the table it leans the same way by less -- 0.985 against 1.077 -- and that record cannot be read for this, because there the unit's peak stands 0.0262 octaves below where the frequency table puts it, a third of a band, and the residual that offset leaves is -0.45 dB below the top and 0.62 dB above it -- bigger than the thing being read.

run.held: the centre byte at an entry the frequency run showed standing in its own band -- 96 or 112 -- with the gain this byte shapes at full and the type's other three gains at their centres, which is the hold the two records already scored were taken under
run.stimulus: a note held through the effect, its takes read as the energy of each twelfth octave against the run's own flat repeats
run.why: One record already leans to 4.5 at every band that can tell the two apart, and the other is read at a centre the unit puts a third of a band from the table's entry. A second centre with no offset in it is what turns a lean into a reading.

separated_by.why_it_is_not_taken_as_settled: The bands it is read at were chosen because that is where the two differ, and they were chosen after the ranking came back tied. That is the right place to read and the wrong order to have chosen it in, so what it is entitled to is a lean and a queue entry rather than a refutation.

alternatives.ruled_out_by: The run this alternative named was made, at two centres rather than one, and the observable it named answers. At the fourth entry of the frequency table the unit's peak stands 0.0047 octaves from where the model puts it, 0.06 of a band and the cleanest centre this archive has read, so the residual that offset leaves is 0.18 dB against a gap of 0.60 dB. At the narrowest entry the two readings are told apart at 13 bands, the run's own floor at the widest of them is 0.13 dB, and the unit is nearer 4.5 at every one of them: 0.165 dB root mean square against 0.582. The record swept at the bottom of the table says the same and clears the same bar (0.204 against 0.544, nearer at every one of 14). What makes this a refutation rather than the lean it was is the order: the bands, the prediction either way and the margin were written here before the takes were made. data/units/roland-sc8850-01/efx-bands/01-00-08-the-width-at-two-more-centres-400-in-twelfths.json.

refuted_by: A width byte read at the narrowest setting, at a centre the frequency table places in its own band, coming back at the printed figure rather than half of it. Or the same setting returning two different widths at two centres, which would make the entries coefficient sets stored per centre and not a table. Or a setting past the fifth returning anything the first five do not.

compared_against.generated_from: data/units/roland-sc8850-01/index.json, filtered to the efx-bands records of type 01 00 whose swept address is a mid width byte, at the finest resolution published for each
compared_against.why_the_nulls_are_scored: The frequency class drops its null controls, because a byte swept through a gain left at its centre has no feature to put anywhere and there is no place to be right or wrong about. A width byte swept the same way has something to be wrong about: it must not widen anything, and a candidate that renders a peak into a record where the unit showed none has contradicted a reading rather than earned a residual. All four are answered and none is over the floor.

settings.40 03 0B: Three of the five on the type's other mid section

domain.outside: Every gain other than the full boost these runs hold. The five entries are read as the shape at the top of the gain's range, and the shape at half that gain is not what any fixed-width section gives -- measured on two combination types and about forty per cent narrower than the full-boost shape predicts, which is a property of how the gain byte reaches the section and is not this table's. Every centre except the four asked. The five other types the page prints this same list against, of which two are read at the same five settings and folded in without being scored.

residual.why: A decibel residual over the band profile is the instrument this byte is visible in, which is the opposite of the byte next door: a width changes the profile by most of the peak's height on its flanks and leaves its top alone, so the residual is largest exactly where the candidates differ. The two classes read the same records with two instruments on purpose.

gross.why: The median residual over the span the effect commands, taken as the worst of the records scored. A rejection bound and not a target: below it the residual is reported and never optimised, because no candidate is decided by it.

qualitative.why: Properties the unit's readings have that the model's readings must have too. No arithmetic over a residual rescues a model that cuts where the unit boosts.

power.why: The runner-up in the catalogue, scored on the same records, and whether it leans or contradicts a property where the winner does neither. The decoy is not chosen -- it is whichever candidate came second, so a strawman cannot be put up in its place. A class holding one candidate is a catalogue that is unfinished, which is a finding and not a pass.

records_the_run_did_not_reach.why: The profile had not levelled off where the band set ended, so the corner the model takes from this record is a lower bound. A residual leaning across the bands is that bound leaning. Answering it needs a stimulus that reaches further, not a different model.

breakdown.why: A point worse than 0.5 of the span is a failure at that point rather than error at it. A residual that leans with the setting or with frequency is pointing at a structure the model does not have; one that does not is pointing at the room and the converters, and is not made smaller by anything this project can do.

reproduces.what_the_verdict_means_here: `equivalent_under_this_test` is the power gate reporting that the runner-up neither leans nor contradicts a property, and the runner-up is the same table with one entry moved eleven per cent. Four of the five entries are not in question between the two, and everything that does not halve the printed list is beaten by six times the residual and by three leaning records. The verdict is about the fifth entry, and the fifth entry is no longer in question -- it is settled below, by the reading this claim wrote down as the thing that would settle it, at a centre the section stands six hundredths of a band from. A profile-wide residual cannot carry that reading and the verdict does not pretend to: eleven per cent of one entry of five is a fiftieth of a profile, which is under this gate's own floor. The gate is reporting the limit of the gate.

the_per_setting_residual.read_as: Setting by setting, the median residual in decibels for the halved table and for the printed one. The halved table sits between four and fifteen hundredths of a decibel at every setting of both records; the printed one is at a decibel and a half at the widest setting and closes on the halved table as the entries narrow, because a table twice too narrow is wrong by a factor and a factor is smallest where the peak is smallest.

the_same_table_at_two_centres.what: The five entries were read with the centre byte at 64 and again at 0, which the frequency table puts an octave and a half apart.
the_same_table_at_two_centres.read_as: Both records return the same five widths and the same winner, and no candidate's ranking moves between them. That is what says the five numbers are a table multiplied into whatever the centre gives, rather than five coefficient sets stored against one centre -- and it is the one thing in this class a candidate cannot be made to fit by choosing five numbers, because the five are the same at both.

the_two_mid_sections_and_two_more_types.read_as: The type's second mid section answers at three of the five settings with the first's figures. Two combination types carry the same section at their own addresses and were read at all five: one of them at the centre this type's own width run held, so its half-power edges can be laid over that run's without a correction, and they are the same bands at all five settings. Four of the eight slots the page prints this list against now answer alike.

what_the_records_own_reading_gives.what: The width computed straight out of each record's published half-gain pair, which is the readout this claim is not resting on.
what_the_records_own_reading_gives.read_as: Four of the five land within two per cent of the halved table. The fifth reads 3.45 where the claim says 4.5, and that is the reading and not the unit: the pair it is computed from is quantised to the band set and is read off a profile the band energy has already smoothed, and both widen a peak this narrow. A model rendered through the same reading is smoothed the same way and lands on 4.5, which is the whole reason the comparison is made that way round. A candidate whose five entries are these five numbers is kept out of the ranking: it has one free entry per setting and could not have come out wrong.

what_this_does_not_close.what: What the section does at a gain below the full one these runs hold.
what_this_does_not_close.why: Every record scored here holds the gain the width shapes at full, so what the five entries are is read at one gain. Two combination types were swept through their gain with the width resting at the middle entry, and at six decibels the peak comes back about forty per cent narrower than a section of that width gives at twelve -- the same way on the boost and on the cut. A fixed-width section does not do that, so something about how the gain byte reaches the section is not a gain in a peaking filter.
what_this_does_not_close.what_would: Nothing further. The run this named -- the width byte at a gain six steps inside the window -- was not needed: what answers it is the gain byte swept through the middle of its own window with the width resting, which the archive already held, read for the width of the feature rather than for its height.
what_this_does_not_close.what_it_turned_out_to_be: The byte does not build the section at the gain it names. It blends one stored full-scale section against the dry path, so the width this claim identifies is the width of the stored section and the width at any other setting of the gain follows from the blend. The five entries are unchanged and so is the reading that they are the printed figures halved: every record this claim was scored on holds its gain at full, which is exactly where the stored section is.

what_this_does_not_close.why: The two differ by at most six tenths of a decibel at one band and by nothing at the top of the peak. One of the two records leans to 4.5 at every band that can tell them apart; the other is read at a centre the unit puts a third of a band away from the table's entry, and the residual that leaves is larger than the difference being read.
what_this_does_not_close.what_would: The same five settings at a third centre, chosen from the entries the frequency run showed standing in their own band.

what_this_does_not_close.what: The four other types the page prints this list against, and the third slot of the two that are read.
what_this_does_not_close.why: Eight slots print it. Four answer alike -- two on the standalone type and two combination types read at all five settings -- and the four left are carried by nothing but this claim's own reading that one table serves the list.
what_this_does_not_close.what_would: One sweep on a type from outside the guitar family the two folded types both come from.

what_this_does_not_close.what: Why the unit's peak at the narrowest setting stands a third of a band below the entry the frequency table gives, at the middle centre and not at the bottom one.
what_this_does_not_close.why: It is under what the frequency class resolves -- half a band -- so that class reports the entry as landing in its own band and is not wrong to. It shows here because the narrowest width is the only reading in the archive fine enough for a third of a band to be most of a residual.
what_this_does_not_close.what_would: The narrowest width at several centres, read as where the peak sits rather than how wide it is, which is the frequency class's instrument applied to the setting that sharpens it.

what_it_would_change: A renderer given the printed figures makes every peak of every equaliser and of six combination types half as wide as the unit's, at every setting of the byte. That is a decibel and a half of profile at the widest setting and it is the most audible of the three mid bytes to get wrong, because a width error moves the flanks of the peak and leaves its top -- so the parameter sounds as though it is doing the right thing at the frequency it is set to.
a_note_on_what_it_replaces: The equaliser type's own model already carried two candidates differing in exactly this, one holding the printed figures and one holding five numbers computed out of the record's half-gain pairs. The second was right about four entries by accident of being a readout and wrong about the fifth by the width of the reading it was computed from. Both are superseded here by a table that was not fitted: 0.25, 0.5, 1.0, 2.0 and 4.5 is the printed list halved and nothing in it was chosen.

read_at_the_centre_the_section_stands_ne.what: The width byte swept at all five entries at two more centres, to answer the observable this claim's last standing alternative named. Twenty takes. The two records are separate because the null control beside each was taken with the gain the byte shapes at its centre, which is a different held block.
read_at_the_centre_the_section_stands_ne.why_a_record_has_to_earn_the_reading: The reading is 0.6 dB at one band of a profile that spans thirteen, so a centre the section does not stand on swamps it. The record swept with its centre in the middle of the table stands 0.0262 octaves off the entry the model renders and that offset alone leaves 0.62 dB, which is as large as the thing being read; it was refused. The record swept at the bottom stands 0.0101 and leaves 0.25; it was read. The bar is those two and not these: the offset may leave under half the gap the two readings differ by at their widest band, which admits the one that was read and refuses the one that was refused. It was applied to the new records and it refused one of them.
read_at_the_centre_the_section_stands_ne.which_centres_and_why_those: Read off the sixteen-entry readout published beside the frequency class, which gives every entry as this rig measured it against the printed series the model renders. The fourth entry is the nearest of all sixteen and the thirteenth is the one the queue entry named; they are 0.013 octaves apart in that readout, a sixth of a band and inside the scatter of the fit that produced both figures, so choosing between them there would have been choosing on a difference the readout cannot carry. Both were asked and each record answers for its own offset, measured in the record rather than carried into it.

the_centre_that_answers.centre_byte: 40 03 07 = 24, the fourth entry of the frequency table

the_centre_that_does_not.centre_byte: 40 03 07 = 96, the thirteenth entry of the frequency table
the_centre_that_does_not.read_as: Refused, and it is the centre the queue entry named. It stands half as far off its entry as the centre that was refused before it and still leaves more than the bar allows, which says the bar is not a proxy for the offset and that a centre has to be read rather than picked. Its ranking is reported and not counted: it leans the same way as the two that answer (0.361 against 0.533) but the unit is not nearer at every band, which is what a record with an offset in it looks like.

read_at_the_centre_the_section_stands_ne.and_the_nulls: A null control beside each centre, the width byte at the entry in dispute with the gain it shapes at its centre. Both come back at the flat repeats' own level to a tenth of a decibel, and every candidate stays inside the floor on both -- so no reading here is putting a peak where the unit shows none.
read_at_the_centre_the_section_stands_ne.what_it_does_not_settle: The entry at every centre. Four of the sixteen have been asked and the two that can be read agree; the other twelve are not asked, and the one that was asked and refused is refused for its offset rather than for what it said.

the_round_that_read_a_fourth_type_carryi.what_was_asked: Which of two readings the first round could not choose between: that a byte past the fifth printed step returns the first entry, or that it returns whatever entry the slot powers up in. On the type this claim was fitted on those are the same entry, which the round said in its own words and left open.
the_round_that_read_a_fourth_type_carryi.why_a_fourth_type_answers_it: Because the ambiguity is a coincidence of one slot and not a property of the table, so what breaks it is a slot carrying the same table and powering up somewhere else. An eight-band graphic prints the same five figures at the same five hex values under a different name -- the page calls it a width where the parametric equaliser calls it a Q -- and it powers up at the third entry rather than the first. Nothing had to be built for it: the byte was swept through its printed steps and past them on takes the same stage reads.
the_round_that_read_a_fourth_type_carryi.what_it_returned: Four of the five entries are the same to the twelfth of an octave the reading steps in: 2.583, 1.417, 0.750 and 0.417 octaves between the half-gain points at bytes one to four, against the same four figures on the type this claim was fitted on. The widest entry differs -- 3.917 against 4.167 -- and that is the entry whose half-gain points fall outside the band set, so where they are read is set by where the reading stops. Past the fifth step, bytes five, sixty-four and a hundred and twenty-seven all return 0.417, which is the fifth entry and not the first.
the_round_that_read_a_fourth_type_carryi.what_it_settles: Both readings the first round left standing are wrong about this slot, and one of them stays right about the other. Past-the-printed is not the first entry here: the first is 3.917 octaves and what comes back is 0.417. It is not the power-on entry either: this byte powers up at the third, which is 1.417, measured on the same run from takes with nothing written to any of the type's bytes. So the rule is local to the slot. On the type this claim rests on the two readings still cannot be told apart, and nothing here changes that -- what changes is that the question is now known to have a per-slot answer rather than one waiting to be found.
the_round_that_read_a_fourth_type_carryi.why_this_is_not_a_refutation: The claim names its own refutation as a setting past the fifth returning anything the first five do not. The fifth is one of the five. What the table holds is unchanged and now stands on a fourth type; what moves is a sentence about what a byte outside the table does, which was already carrying its own ambiguity.
the_round_that_read_a_fourth_type_carryi.why_the_type_is_not_added_to_the_scope: This claim's addresses are the width slots of the types it was fitted on, and a reader who takes its types against its addresses would credit it with three parameters of the new type that it says nothing about: two of those addresses are that type's sixth and seventh band gains and one it does not print. A claim's reach is the printed signature it was fitted on and never a column of the address space. The new type's own claim names its width byte, and that is where the parameter is counted.
the_round_that_read_a_fourth_type_carryi.what_it_does_not_close: Why the two slots differ. Holding at the last entry is what a clamp does and returning the first is what a mask or a rejected value does, but the takes here say which entry comes back and not what put it there, and one type doing each is as consistent with two pieces of code as with one reached two ways. Nor does it reopen the halving: the four entries that agree agree at the figures this claim already published.
